He singled out the Prophet ﷺ with the address and generalised the instruction. It is narrated that some people said: "We know the waiting period (ʿiddah, the prescribed period of waiting after divorce or widowhood) of women who have menstrual cycles (qurūʾ). The meaning of "if you are in doubt" is: if their ruling becomes unclear to you and you do not know how they should observe the waiting period, then this is their ruling. It is also said: if you are in doubt about the women who have reached the age of despair (yaʾs from menstruation), which they have estimated as sixty years or fifty-five, whether the blood they see is menstrual blood (ḥayḍ) or irregular bleeding (istiḥāḍah)?

"And those who have not menstruated" are the young girls. The meaning is: their waiting period is three months, and the words were omitted because what was mentioned indicates them.

He has another route connected through ʿUbayd ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Maʿqil, who said: "I witnessed ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him..." and he mentioned something similar.]

It is reported from ʿAbd Allāh: "Whoever wishes, I will curse him (in dispute): the shorter Sūrat al-Nisāʾ was revealed after the one in al-Baqarah." [It is narrated by al-Bukhārī, Abū Dāwūd, al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Mājah through Masrūq; al-Bukhārī did not mention its beginning. ʿAbd al-Razzāq added that he said this when it reached him that ʿAlī had said: "It is in the later of the two terms."] That is, this wording is general concerning pregnant women.

The meaning is: whoever fears Allah in acting upon what Allah has revealed of these rulings, and preserves the rights that are obligatory upon him concerning what was mentioned, such as providing housing, refraining from harm, maintenance for pregnant women, paying the wages of nursing mothers, and other matters, he has earned the expiation of his misdeeds and a great reward.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 65, verse 6–7:

﴿Lodge them﴾ and what follows is an explanation of the taqwa (God-consciousness) stipulated in His words, ﴿And whoever is mindful of God﴾, as if it were said: How are we to act with taqwa regarding the women in ʿidda (waiting period)? So it was said: ﴿Lodge them﴾. If you ask: What is the min in ﴿from where you dwell﴾? I say: it is the partitive min, whose part is omitted, meaning: lodge them in a place from where you dwell, i.e., part of the place of your dwelling, like His words, ﴿they should lower some of their gaze﴾, i.e., part of their gaze. Qatada said: If there is only one house, then lodge her in one of its corners. If you ask: What about His words ﴿from your means﴾? I say: it is an appositive (ʿatf bayan) to ﴿from where you dwell﴾ and an explanation of it, as if it were said: lodge them in a place from your dwelling that is within your capacity. Al-wajd means ability and capacity; it is also read with the three vowel-forms. Lodging and maintenance are obligatory for every divorced woman. According to Malik and al-Shafiʿi, the irrevocably divorced woman is entitled only to lodging, and she has no maintenance. According to al-Hasan and Hammad: she has neither maintenance nor lodging, based on the hadith of Fatima bint Qays: that her husband divorced her irrevocably, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to her: "You have no lodging and no maintenance." (Muslim reported it through several chains from her, and in one narration: "He did not assign to her lodging or maintenance," and in another: "You have no maintenance and no lodging," and in another: "My husband divorced me three times.") And ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him) said: "We will not abandon the Book of our Lord and the Sunna of our Prophet for the word of a woman who perhaps forgot or was mistaken. I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: 'She is entitled to lodging and maintenance.'" (Muslim, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i reported it through Abu Ishaq, who said: "I was with al-Aswad, and al-Sha'bi was with us in the mosque when al-Sha'bi related the hadith of Fatima bint Qays. Al-Aswad took a handful of pebbles and threw them at him and said: 'Woe to you! Do you relate the like of this?' ʿUmar said: 'We will not abandon the Book of our Lord and the Sunna of our Prophet for the word of a woman who perhaps memorized or forgot.'")

﴿And do not harm them﴾, i.e., do not use harm against them, ﴿to constrain them﴾ in the dwelling by some means: such as bringing in someone who is not agreeable to them, or occupying their place, or other things, ﴿until you force them to leave﴾. It was said: it is that he takes her back when two days of her waiting period remain, in order to make her situation difficult. It was also said: it is that he compels her to ransom herself from him. If you ask: If every divorced woman, in your view, is owed maintenance, what is the point of the condition in His words, ﴿And if they are pregnant, then spend on them﴾? [Here the commentary quotes its source: the verses from "Lodge them from where you dwell..." to "...if they are pregnant...". Ahmad said: It is not hidden from anyone who reflects on these verses that the irrevocably divorced woman who is not pregnant has no maintenance, because the verses were brought to explain the obligation, so they obligated lodging for every woman in waiting period mentioned earlier and obligated nothing beyond it, then excepted the pregnant women, specifying for them the obligation of maintenance until they give birth to their burden, and after this explanation there is no further explanation. To say, after this, that maintenance is obligatory for every divorced woman in waiting period, whether pregnant or not, clearly contradicts the structure of the verse. Al-Zamakhshari supported the position of Abu Hanifa and said: the purpose of singling out pregnant women is that the pregnancy may last long, so someone might suppose that maintenance is not owed over its length; therefore they were singled out to remove this illusion. Al-Zamakhshari's aim in this is to make the specification serve this purpose, so that it would not carry an implication of dropping maintenance for non-pregnant women, since Abu Hanifa equates them all in the obligation of maintenance.]] I say: its benefit is that the period of pregnancy may be long, so someone might think maintenance falls away once the period of waiting for a non-pregnant woman has passed, so this illusion is negated. Most scholars hold that she has no maintenance, since there is consensus that a man who is compelled to maintain a wife or a young child is not required to be supported from his property after his death; so likewise the pregnant woman. It is reported from ʿAli, ʿAbd Allah and a group that they obligated her maintenance.

﴿And if they suckle for you﴾, meaning these divorced women, if they nurse a child for you, whether from them or from others, after the bond of marriage has ended, ﴿then give them their wages﴾. Their ruling in this matter is the ruling of wet-nurses (aẓʾār; sing. ẓi'r, the woman who nurses another's child; plural also ẓu'ār and ẓu'ūr, as in the Sihah). According to Abu Hanifa and his companions, may God be pleased with them, it is not permitted to hire a woman to nurse when the child is her own, as long as he has not been weaned; it is permitted according to al-Shafiʿi.

﴿Consult together in kindness﴾: the verb ʾitamara means the same as ta'ammara (to consult), as ishtawara means to take counsel. It is said: the people consulted together (i'tamara al-qawm wa ta'ammarū) when some of them commanded others. The meaning: let some of you command others, and the address is to the fathers and mothers. ﴿In kindness﴾ means in what is good, which is forbearance: the father should not haggle and the mother should not obstruct, for the child is theirs jointly, and they are partners in it and in the obligation of care for it. ﴿And if you disagree﴾, ﴿then another woman will suckle for him﴾: another will be found, and there will be no lack of a wet-nurse other than the mother to nurse him. There is in this a touch of reproach to the mother for obstinacy, as you say to someone whose help you request and who delays: "Someone else will do it." [Mahmud said: "In His words, ﴿And if you disagree, then another will suckle for him﴾, there is a reproach to the mother for obstinacy, as you say to someone you ask for a need and who delays..." Ahmad said: He singled out the mother for reproach because what is offered on her part is her milk for her child, which is not regarded as valuable or withheld by custom, especially a mother toward her child; this is not so with what is offered by the father, which is money, customarily withheld. It is also read ﴿li-yunfiq﴾ with a fatha, meaning: We have legislated that so that he may spend.

Ibn Abi ʿAbla read: ﴿qadar﴾ ... ﴿God will bring about after hardship ease﴾, a promise to the poor of that time by opening the doors of provision for them, or to the poor husbands if they spend what they are able to, without falling short.

**Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on Surah 65, verses 8–11:**

﴿عَتَتْ عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّها﴾ meaning: it rebelled against the command of its Lord, turning away from it with defiance and obstinacy. ﴿حِساباً شَدِيداً﴾ meaning: a severe reckoning, through exhaustive scrutiny and questioning. ﴿عَذاباً نُكْراً﴾ meaning: a terrible punishment. It is also recited as ﴿نكرا﴾ (munkaran), meaning: a great, dreadful punishment.

The intended meaning is the reckoning of the Hereafter and its punishment, and what they will taste there of disaster and suffer of loss. It is expressed in the past tense, as in His saying ﴿وَنادى أَصْحابُ الْجَنَّةِ﴾ and ﴿وَنادى أَصْحابُ النَّارِ﴾ and similar verses, because what is awaited of Allah's promise and threat is, in reality, already settled, and what is certain to happen is treated as having already happened.

His saying ﴿أَعَدَّ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ عَذاباً شَدِيداً﴾ is a repetition of the threat and an explanation that it is something awaited. It is as if He said: Allah has prepared this punishment for them, so let it be a reason for you, O people of understanding (﴿أُولِي الْأَلْبابِ﴾) among the believers, to be mindful of Allah and wary of His punishment.

It is also permissible that the intended meaning is the counting of their evil deeds and the exact accounting of them against them in this world, their recording in the scrolls of the recording angels, and the punishment they suffered in this life.

It is also possible that ﴿عَتَتْ﴾ and what is joined to it is an attribute (ṣifah) of the town (qaryah).

As for ﴿أَعَدَّ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ﴾, it is the answer to ﴿كَأَيِّنْ﴾. ﴿رَسُولًا﴾ is Jibril, may Allah's blessings be upon him. It is a substitution (badal, apposition) for ﴿ذِكْراً﴾, because he is described as one who recites the verses of Allah, so his sending down is in the sense of the sending down of the Reminder. Hence it is valid for him to be a substitution for it.

[[Al-Zamakhshari mentions six possibilities regarding ﴿رَسُولًا﴾: the substitution of the messenger for the Reminder, because his sending down is in the sense of sending down the Reminder... etc. Ahmad (Ibn al-Munayyir) says: According to these last two possibilities, it is an object (mafʿūl), either by means of the omitted verb or by means of the verbal noun. According to the four preceding ones, it is a substitution (badal). And Allah, glorified and exalted, knows best.]]

Alternatively, ﴿الذِّكْر﴾ may be understood as honour (sharaf), from His saying ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَذِكْرٌ لَكَ وَلِقَوْمِكَ﴾, and so he is substituted for it, as if he were himself an honour: either because he is an honour to the one to whom he was sent down, or because he is of great glory and honour with Allah, as in His saying ﴿عِنْدَ ذِي الْعَرْشِ مَكِينٍ﴾. Or he is treated as the Reminder because of his great remembrance of Allah and his worship, as if he were himself a reminder.

Or it may be understood as: one who possesses a reminder, that is, a noble angel mentioned in the heavens and among all nations.

Or His saying ﴿أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْكُمْ ذِكْراً﴾ implies "he sent," so it is as if it were said: He sent a messenger. Or the verbal noun ﴿ذِكْراً﴾ governs ﴿رَسُولًا﴾ in the manner of a verbal noun governing its objects, meaning: Allah sent down that He would remind of a messenger, or that He would mention a messenger.

﴿رَسُولٌ﴾ is also recited in the nominative, as: he is a messenger.

**Translation:**

Allah is He who created (ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ) — the subject (mubtada') and predicate (khabar), i.e. the grammatical construction "Allah" as subject and "who created" as predicate.

It is also read as *mithlahunna* with the accusative (naṣb), in coordination with *sab' samawat* ("seven heavens"), and with the nominative (raf') as a new subject (mubtada'), its predicate being *min al-ard* ("and of the earth").

It has been said: there is no verse in the Qur'an that indicates the earths are seven except this one.

It has also been said: between every two heavens is a distance of five hundred years' journey, the thickness of each heaven is likewise, and the earths are like the heavens.

*Yatanazzalu al-amru baynahunna* ("the command descends among them"), i.e., the command of Allah and His judgment proceed among them, and His sovereignty takes effect within them.

From Qatada: in every heaven and in every earth there is a creation of His creation, a command of His command, and a decree of His decree.

It has been said: it is what He arranges within them of the wonders of His management.

It is also read *yunzilu al-amr*.

From Ibn 'Abbas: Nafi' ibn al-Azraq asked him, "Is there any creation beneath the earths?" He said, "Yes." He said, "And what is the creation?" He said, "Either angels or jinn."

*Li-ta'lamu* ("that you may know") is read with the *ta'* (second person) and with the *ya'* (third person).

From the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surat al-Talaq dies upon the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."
